transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Nice to meet you too. Um, well, what finally made me ask for help is that I just keep forgetting little things I normally handle without a problem. 

I'll forget to return phone calls, or I'll forget to turn in a registration form, or I'll completely miss stopping for an errand on the way home from work. It's just been happening enough lately that I figured I should come in and talk to someone about it.
Aside from the forgetfulness, have you been feeling down, depressed, or hopeless lately?

No, not really. I mean, I get a bit frustrated with myself when I drop the ball on things, but I haven't been feeling depressed or hopeless at all. My mood is honestly fine, it's just the memory stuff that's bothering me.
Have you struggled with this kind of forgetfulness and difficulty staying organized your entire life, or is this a relatively new development?

It's pretty much been my whole life, honestly. Um, even back in elementary school, I was always the kid who forgot permission slips, or I'd somehow lose my finished homework in the bottom of my backpack. I always needed my mom or my teachers to remind me step by step just to get my projects done. So, yeah, it's definitely not a new development.

latest_inference.note: The patient's report of lifelong symptoms (forgetfulness, organizational difficulties) starting in childhood strongly aligns with ADHD. Given the lack of mood symptoms (ruling out major depression) and the duration of the symptoms, other transient causes or anxiety-related memory issues are less likely.
